_comment: Single source of truth for every mobile budget `bun run bench:mobile` gates on.
Edit the numbers here; nothing in src/ carries a threshold of its own.
source: 'contract' means native/CONTRACT.md states the number.
source: 'allowance' means this harness declares the ceiling because the contract
names the behaviour without a number. An allowance is a promise, so keep the
reason in `note` and raise it only with a measured justification.
'omit' on a row means measure and report but never gate.

bootstrap_to_snapshot_warm_ms.note: bootstrap() to first synchronous snapshot(), warm: under 5 ms.

bootstrap_to_snapshot_cold_ms.note: bootstrap() to first synchronous snapshot(), cold: under 15 ms.

cold_start_overhead_ms.note: Cold-start overhead attributable to c15t: under 10 ms. Measured as the cold bootstrap-to-first-snapshot span, which is the only work c15t adds to launch before the first read.

commit_ack_no_network_ms.note: Consent action to native commit acknowledged, no network: under 50 ms.

rerenders_per_consent_change.note: React rerenders per consent change: at most one per subscribed component.

rerenders_per_unchanged_event.note: Derived from the contract: the module never sends a snapshot JavaScript already holds, and selector subscriptions rerender only when the selected value changes, so an unchanged snapshot event must cost zero rerenders.

snapshot_object_identities.note: snapshot() and isAllowed() must not allocate a new snapshot per call. Counted as the number of distinct snapshot objects observed across repeated reads: one object means none was built per call.

native_bootstrap_to_snapshot_warm_ms.note: bootstrap() to first synchronous snapshot(), warm, on the native core: under 5 ms.

native_bootstrap_to_snapshot_cold_ms.note: bootstrap() to first synchronous snapshot(), cold, on the native core: under 15 ms.

native_hydrate_envelope_ms.note: Native hydrate from a stored envelope: under 3 ms for a realistic payload.

native_commit_ack_no_network_ms.note: Native consent action to commit acknowledged, no network: under 50 ms.

native_snapshot_object_identities.note: The native read must not build a snapshot per call, counted as distinct snapshot objects across repeated reads.

native_snapshot_read_us.note: No contract number for the read itself. 2 us is the guard against a synchronous read that starts doing work.

policy_evaluation_us.note: The contract sets no ceiling for evaluation alone; the native benches already assert this one. 50 us guards against a blow-up in the selector path without pretending to be a contract number.

snapshot_read_us.note: No contract number; the contract forbids per-call allocation and I/O instead. 2 us is a guard for a synchronous read that starts touching something it should not.

idle_cpu_percent.note: Quiet window with one active subscription: no timer, no poll, no network. 2 % of one core allows the periodic reachability hook and rules out a busy loop.

idle_rss_growth_bytes.note: Resident-set growth across the quiet window: 256 KiB allows the allocator's own slack and rejects a per-tick leak.

js_shipped_bytes.note: Unpacked JavaScript in the @c15t/react-native tarball. 96 KiB is a ceiling for the boundary layer, which holds no kernel, no translations, and no policy engine.

js_shipped_gzip_bytes.note: Gzipped JavaScript the tarball ships. 24 KiB is the ceiling for a boundary layer: no kernel, no translations, no policy engine, no UI components in the public entry.

ios_binary_bytes.note: Bytes C15tCore adds to an iOS binary, measured as the linked __TEXT plus __DATA of the arm64 slice. 1 MiB is the ceiling for the Swift core with no IAB.

ios_binding_bytes.note: TurboModule binding bytes on iOS. 256 KiB is the ceiling for a Codegen spec, a JSON marshalling layer, and an event emitter, with no consent logic in it.

android_binary_bytes.note: Bytes the Kotlin core plus the bridge add to an Android app, measured as the uncompressed class bytes of the release artifacts. 1 MiB matches the iOS ceiling for the same engine.

js_hydrate_envelope_ms.note: The contract's 3 ms hydrate budget, applied to the JavaScript decode of the stored envelope.

jsx_global_reference_files.note: Built files that call `React.createElement` without importing React. Zero, because nothing defines a React global in a React Native app and the first render throws.

package_manifest_parse_errors.note: Whether `packages/react-native/package.json` parses. Zero, because a manifest that is not valid JSON cannot be resolved by any Node consumer.

native_is_allowed_us.note: No contract number for the read itself. Same 2 us guard as the snapshot read: the contract's requirement here is that neither read touches I/O.

policy_apply_per_rule_set_us.note: Applying one rule set through the reference evaluator: build the kernel, feed it the fixture's /init body, read the snapshot back. The contract sets no number for this span and it is a wider one than the native `policy_evaluation_us` rows, which evaluate in isolation. 100 us is the regression guard the first measured run supported: 17-24 us across eight rule sets, so this trips on a 4x blow-up rather than on sampling noise.
